title: Order Network rerun claim rollback safely
summary: Persist a Network CSV rerun row rollback before releasing its exact in-flight registry owner, and fail closed when either rollback side cannot reach the intended state.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W01-023. The previous registry-first rollback could free the duplicate-command guard and then fail to roll back the durable batch row, leaving a claimed row stranded without registry ownership.
behavior_before: Network rerun claim rollback removed the in-memory registry entry first. A missing/corrupt batch, batch read error, or atomic batch write failure then left the durable row claimed while registry ownership was absent, permitting conflicting reclaim behavior after persistence or restart.
behavior_after: Rollback verifies the exact durable row claim, atomically persists that row as pending/claimable, and only then releases the exact registry owner. Batch failures retain the active registry claim; a rejected registry release is surfaced while the retained claim continues to quarantine duplicate work.
tests_added: tests/python/desktop/test_network_rerun_claims.py: injected batch read and write failures preserve exact registry ownership across persisted-state reload, and a clean retry converges the row and registry.
tests/python/desktop/test_network_rerun_claims.py: response delivery plus batch rollback-write failure preserves the durable claimed row and persisted registry owner across restart.
tests/python/desktop/test_network_rerun_claims.py: rejected registry release after durable row rollback retains the duplicate-blocking registry quarantine and raises an explicit failure.
